~CHAPTER 25!~
This year I count my blessings and I’m indeed surprised by what the Lord has done! It’s been a whole 25years of God’s amazing faithfulness. Grace has carried me through even when it felt undeserving God has proven himself over and over in my life, even in the littlest things.

Being so big on gratitude, when I look back at how far I’ve come, I’m grateful for all the things I’ve been through, all the life lessons I’m learning, the family I’m blessed to call mine, the friends/people I’m surrounded with and I say ABBA THANK YOU 🙏 

The past year stretched me, almost broke me in ways I just couldn’t explain to anyone but I’m glad I always retrace my steps back to God, who always helps me by assuring me through His words.

 I might not be there yet, but I trust that God is doing His thing with me already which is why I titled this Chapter- “AGE LIKE A BLOOMING ROSE”🌹 It’s the age I grow older with grace, beauty, vibrancy, love, value and wisdom while embracing personal development in all seasons without fading. 
With all that said, I wish myself a rosy journey ahead 🥂 

Happy birthday Ogunyomi Olasubomi Olasewa Khairat Asake 💜
 God is about to work more wonders with you! 🎉😌

Twenty-Four Years of Wisdom: 

To my newborn self, just breathe and know you are already a miracle. 🕊️ At one, your curiosity is a superpower that will help you survive. 🎈 For age two, keep reaching for the things that make you feel small moments of joy. 🧸 At three, your voice matters even when it feels like no one is listening. 📣 For four-year-old me, it is okay to hide in your imagination when the world gets too loud. 🎨 At five, you are not responsible for the big people’s feelings around you. 🛡️ For age six, keep your heart soft even when things feel hard. 🌸 At seven, your sensitive soul is a gift, not a burden. 💎 For eight-year-old me, you are allowed to take up space in this world. 🌍 At nine, find the stories and poems that make you feel less alone. 📖 For age ten, you are so much braver than you realize. 🦁 At eleven, trust your gut when it tells you something isn’t right. 🧩 For twelve-year-old me, you don’t have to earn love; you deserve it just for existing. 💝 At thirteen, this awkwardness is just the beginning of a beautiful unfolding. ✨ For fourteen, it’s okay to be angry about what you’ve had to endure. 🔥 At fifteen, hold on to your dreams of a different life because they are coming true. 🌠 For sixteen-year-old me, you are finding your own path, and that is terrifying and wonderful. 🛣️ At seventeen, you are almost at the finish line of a very long race. 🏁 For eighteen, welcome to the first day of the rest of your life as your own person. 🎓 At nineteen, it’s okay to change your mind and start over as many times as you need. 🔄 For twenty-year-old me, healing is not a straight line, so be patient with your heart. 📈 At twenty-one, find the people who see your light and cherish it. 👯 For twenty-two, your career as a caregiver is proof of the immense love you have to give. 🎗️ At twenty-three, prioritize your peace above everything else. 🕯️ And now, at twenty-four, I look in the mirror and see a survivor who is finally learning how to thrive. 🎂🌈

🌟 Chancen durch digitale Bildung – Fragrance Computer Class 🌟
In Kooperation mit Fusion Nepal entsteht im Kathmandu-Tal ein Lernraum, der Menschen neue Perspektiven eröffnet: "Fragrance Computer Class – Digital Skills for Opportunities" 💻✨ Hier erhalten Erwachsene jeden Alters, die am lokalen Arbeitsmarkt bisher kaum Chancen hatten, erstmals Zugang zu digitalem Wissen. Viele von ihnen sitzen zum ersten Mal an einem Laptop – und machen Schritte, die ihre Zukunft nachhaltig verändern können. ✨
📚 Was hier entsteht:
✨ Offene Lernzeiten & strukturierte Computerkurse
✨ Office-Grundlagen, Schreiben, Internetrecherche
✨ Bewerbungs- & Interviewtraining
✨ Zeit- & Selbstmanagement für den Berufsalltag
Und ab dem neuen Schuljahr im April profitieren auch Schüler*innen staatlicher Schulen – mit Zugang zu digitalen Basiskompetenzen und E‑Learning‑Möglichkeiten. 🎒💻
🔥 Warum uns das wichtig ist:
Weil digitale Fähigkeiten heute darüber entscheiden können, ob jemand einen Job findet, sich weiterbilden kann oder neue Hoffnung schöpft. Fusion Nepal schafft einen Ort, an dem genau das möglich wird: Lernen, wachsen, Zukunft entwickeln.
Wir unterstützen die Initiative mit Laptops, Möbeln, Lernmaterialien und der Finanzierung der laufenden Kosten. Doch der entscheidende Schritt kommt von den Menschen selbst: Sie trauen sich zu lernen – und trauen sich, an ihre Zukunft zu glauben. 🌱

text:
If you’ve been following my journey here, you know how deeply I love dance, fashion, and culture. Bringing all of my passions into one with Nach Firiri!

After years of experimenting with different styles and outfits in my dance videos, I always find myself coming back to simple, dance-friendly pieces like kurthis with a flattering fit and sheer sleeves. There’s just something about moving in certain outfits that feels fun…kurthis being one of them especially given the dance style I do.

So I’m starting Nach Firiri with a simple vision: wear your culture, dance freely with it, and proudly carry it everywhere you go! 

I am starting this journey with Maya Collection, which feature simple, dance friendly kurthis inspired by my Nepali roots. I’ve rarely seen Nepali fashion represented on social media in the way it truly deserves. My goal with this first collection is to showcase Nepali culture through both dance and fashion.

Don’t know where this journey will lead, but I am building this with a lot of love for the craft with so many fun ideas in the pipeline. I hope you’ll follow along for the ride.

Nepali Fusion Series: Episode 1. Is this the ultimate Nepalese momo fusion? 👀 

I’m kicking off my new series with a recipe inspired by one of our most beloved Nepali food: momo. Think of this as a “Momo-Taco” fusion.

If you’ve ever struggled with the art of wrapping momo, don’t worry, I’ve got you. This dish gives you all those traditional flavors of momo without the stress. We’re using a juicy pork filling packed with fresh ginger notes, just like my family makes.

We’re taking traditional Nepalese pork filling. And instead of steaming, we’re pan-searing these for that crispy, golden finish. Then, we coat them in a vibrant achaar made from tomato and toasted sesame also known as “Till” in Nepali. It’s quick, it’s punchy, and it tastes like a classic fried pork momo with achaar 🤤.

You’ve seriously got to try this one. You can find the full recipe over on my Substack! Link is in my bio ❤️‍🔥
